cls: NSAID (non-selective COX inhibitor, indole acetic acid derivative)
pharm: Potent anti-inflammatory, analgesic, antipyretic; strong prostaglandin synthesis inhibitor
quick: 25 mg BID-TID (gout 50 mg TID); max ~200 mg/day
Avoid in advanced disease; can cause AKI
BP, renal, LFTs, CBC, GI symptoms
summary: Indomethacin is a potent non-selective NSAID used for rheumatoid arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, osteoarthritis, acute painful shoulder (bursitis/tendinitis), and acute gouty arthritis. It is among the more potent and CNS/GI-toxic NSAIDs and carries an NSAID boxed warning for serious cardiovascular thrombotic and gastrointestinal events. Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration, with food, and monitor blood pressure, renal function, and LFTs.
indications: Moderate to severe rheumatoid arthritis (including acute flares)

dosage.d: 25 mg two or three times daily
dosage.n: May increase by 25-50 mg/day at weekly intervals; lowest effective dose
Reduce dose as pain subsides; discontinue when resolved

admin: Take immediately after meals, with food, milk, or antacid to reduce GI upset
Use lowest effective dose for shortest duration
Swallow extended-release capsules whole; do not crush or chew
Maintain upright posture and adequate fluid intake
moa: Inhibits cyclooxygenase (COX-1 and COX-2), a potent inhibitor of prostaglandin synthesis, reducing prostaglandin-mediated inflammation, pain, and fever in peripheral tissues.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to indomethacin (including anaphylaxis or serious skin reactions)
History of asthma, urticaria, or allergic-type reactions after aspirin or other NSAIDs
Setting of coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery
Third-trimester pregnancy (about 30 weeks gestation and later)
relative: Active GI bleeding or peptic ulcer disease

preg: Avoid use from about 20 weeks gestation (risk of fetal renal dysfunction/oligohydramnios) and avoid at about 30 weeks and later (premature closure of fetal ductus arteriosus). NSAIDs are associated with reversible infertility.
lact: Excreted in breast milk in small amounts; use with caution and weigh importance of drug to the mother.
renal: Monitor renal function; avoid in advanced renal disease unless benefit outweighs risk. Can cause acute kidney injury, fluid retention, and hyperkalemia, especially with dehydration, heart failure, or hepatic impairment.
hepatic: Risk of hepatotoxicity; discontinue if abnormal liver tests persist/worsen or signs of liver disease develop. Use caution in hepatic impairment.

major: Anticoagulants (warfarin) and antiplatelets - synergistic bleeding risk
Other NSAIDs/aspirin - additive GI and renal toxicity
moderate: ACE inhibitors/ARBs/diuretics - reduced antihypertensive effect and renal injury (triple whammy)
interactions.food: Take with food/milk to reduce GI upset
interactions.diagnostics: May elevate LFTs and affect renal function tests; can mask fever/inflammation

counsel: Take with food, milk, or antacid
Use lowest dose for shortest time
Report black/tarry stools or severe abdominal pain
Report chest pain, weakness, or slurred speech
Report yellowing of skin, dark urine, or swelling
Do not use in late pregnancy
pearls: First-line NSAID for acute gout and for closure of patent ductus arteriosus (IV formulation, neonates)
More CNS side effects (headache, dizziness, confusion) than many NSAIDs
Potent prostaglandin inhibitor with relatively high GI toxicity - reserve and limit duration
Often combined with food/antacid and PPI in higher-risk patients
missed: Take when remembered unless near next dose, then skip; do not double up. For scheduled anti-inflammatory regimens, resume usual schedule.
overdose: Nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, drowsiness, disorientation, lethargy; severe cases: GI bleeding, hypertension, AKI, hepatic dysfunction, respiratory depression, seizures, coma. Management: supportive care, activated charcoal if within 1 h of substantial ingestion, monitor renal/hepatic function and GI bleeding; no specific antidote; not effectively removed by dialysis (highly protein bound).
